The author's motive to expose the complexities of patriotism and the heavy cost of war is structurally supported by focusing on characters who must navigate profound moral dilemmas and face the tangible consequences of political decisions. By grounding the narrative in the author's own experiences as a war correspondent, the text uses these character arcs to illustrate how abstract political choices impact individual lives, thereby reinforcing the theme that patriotism is not just an ideal but a burden with real-world repercussions.

The organ that pumps blood is the heart.
